nodes.title: Descents, peaks and valleys of parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, number the $n$ spots $0, \dots, n-1$, and let $f : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ give the preferred spot of each of $n$ cars. Then $f$ is a parking function if and only if, for every spot $k \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, at least $k + 1$ cars $i$ satisfy $f(i) \le k$.
nodes.title: Lower-tail characterization of parking functions

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and number the $n$ spots $0, \dots, n-1$. A map $f : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, giving the preferred spot of each of $n$ cars, is a parking function if it is a partial parking function with $n$ cars and $n$ spots, that is, if for every spot $k$, at most $n - k$ cars $i$ satisfy $f(i) \ge k$.
nodes.title: Parking function

nodes.summary: Let $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and number the $t$ spots $0, \dots, t-1$. A map $f : \{0, \dots, s-1\} \to \{0, \dots, t-1\}$, giving the preferred spot of each of $s$ cars, is a partial parking function if for every spot $k \in \{0, \dots, t-1\}$, at most $t - k$ cars $i$ satisfy $f(i) \ge k$.
nodes.title: Partial parking function
Lucky and displacement statistics of Stirling permutations

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $0 < s \le t$. A partial parking function with $s$ cars and $t$ spots is a map $f : \{0, \dots, s - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, t - 1\}$ such that for every spot $k \in \{0, \dots, t - 1\}$ at most $t - k$ cars $i$ have $f(i) \ge k$. The number of partial parking functions with $s$ cars and $t$ spots is $(t + 1 - s)(t + 1)^{s - 1}$.
nodes.title: Number of partial parking functions
